criteria: The RFP's own stated improvement criteria (per-issue)
Method-level evidence: the targeted process changes and the change is measured, not asserted
cycle: method comparison on the process's own evidence
meta-process.description: RFPs about the method/process itself (intake, visualization, MVT-DoE validation). Segmented individually; each is its own context.
questions: Does this RFP improve the method it targets, per its own stated criteria?
What evidence would distinguish the improved method from the current one?

criteria: Gate admission rubric (panel.json roles, DECISION-MATRIX 1-25: Impact x Importance)
Flywheel confirmed/miss outcomes on delphi:outcomes (#1487) reweight the panel (#1489)
quota-surfaces.description: Free-tier quota surfaces from ops/delphi/surfaces.json plus fly.free_tier. The Delphi lane's home segmentation: gate-scored, flywheel-fed. Untouched by the research segmentation.
questions: Is the surface's quota real, sourced, and still current?
What did the last flywheel outcome change about its weight?
quota-surfaces.surface_pattern: any delphi:rfp surface_id listed in ops/delphi/surfaces.json, plus fly.free_tier

research-silos.cycle: Per participant, per cycle: axes records land in ops/delphi/research-axes.json (+ the outcomes ledger #1487) as the arms produce validated outputs, feature extractions, and — at stage 6 — consensus implementation. First-cycle gate scores (parked 6.69) stand on the filings as history of the admission-rubric artifact, superseded as a status by the participant registration.
research-silos.description: The 12 research silos are Delphi process PARTICIPANTS (owner reclassification 2026-10-28, PR #2039, ops/delphi/research-participants.json) — no longer RFP applicants. Each participant is one segment; its four filings are arms (baseline + rnd/selected/control). The gate does not score participants; participation runs through the comparison-axes cycles (ops/delphi/research-axes.json). Comparison stays WITHIN a segment: arms are compared on the three axes as post-hoc records, and no score, rank, or verdict ever crosses segment lines.
questions: Does the variant's produced output validate against the silo's own contract, where the baseline's did or did not?
Which features does each variant extract that the baseline does not (and vice versa)?
Where do baseline and variants converge on one consensus implementation, and where do they irreconcilably differ?
research-silos.segmentation: per-silo: segment_id = silo.id from ops/delphi/research-silos.json; members = baseline (surface_id == silo.id) + variants (surface_id == silo.id + .rnd|.selected|.control)

doe-components.description: The DoE family's four algorithmic components, registered separately (ops/doe/component-registry.json, PR #1974) and evaluated individually: each component is its own segment and context, scored on its own evidence feeds. Findings loop back as revision PRs or explicit no-change records, same discipline as the criteria loop (#1959). Any component is available as a DoE factorial factor under the generator+tests admission rule.
criteria: role fitness — the component does the one job its registry role states, nothing adjacent
evidence feeds live — the feeds named in the registry entry resolve and carry current data
separation clean — no cross-component state bleed; shared cores are deduplicated references, not copies
questions: does the component still do exactly its registered role?
are its registered evidence feeds live and current?
what did this cycle's findings change — revision PR, or no-change record?
doe-components.cycle: Each component's RFP is scored by the gate cycle on its own segment; findings become revision PRs against the component or an explicit no-change record on its RFP. Cross-component comparison is descriptive only — no aggregate component score.
